title: Neural Signals Generate Clinical Notes in the Wild
claim: A system turns long, unstructured signal recordings into structured expert reports by addressing data scarcity, modality alignment, and long-context challenges.
layout: 3 regions: top input-to-report flow, bottom challenges-to-solution boxes, radar chart right
description: The top row follows an EEG recording on a patient's head and a multichannel waveform. Next comes a neurologist at a monitor with thought bubbles, labelled manual review and report writing. Gray arrows lead to a boxed list of structured report sections such as Impression, Background Activity and Events/Seizures. A bold orange arrow carries the raw recording to a large red CELM label, then on to the report. The bottom left has three red-outlined boxes for challenges: lack of paired data, the EEG-language alignment gap, and privacy with long context. Arrows lead to two orange boxes for benchmark construction, with report, hour and patient counts, and for the model components. A radar chart at the bottom right compares CELM with baselines across metrics.
caption: Overview of CELM, a clinical EEG-to-language foundation model (ELM) for translating long-duration EEG recordings into structured clinical reports. CELM addresses key challenges in EEG report generation, including limited EEG-report data, EEG-language alignment, and long-context EEG modeling. The framework constructs a large-scale EEG-report benchmark and enables direct generation of structured clinical reports from raw EEG recordings.
abstract: Generating clinical reports that summarize abnormal patterns, diagnostic findings, and clinical interpretations from long-term EEG recordings remains labor-intensive. We present CELM, the first clinical EEG-to-Language foundation model capable of summarizing long-duration, variable-length EEG recordings and performing end-to-end clinical report generation at multiple scales. CELM integrates pretrained EEG foundation models with language models to enable scalable multimodal learning. We curate a large-scale clinical EEG dataset containing 9,922 reports paired with approximately 11,000 hours of EEG recordings from 9,048 patients to train CELM, and release the benchmark pipeline, with automated report-structuring, to facilitate future research. Experimental results show that CELM consistently outperforms existing methods across all evaluation settings. Importantly, we further conduct human evaluation with clinical experts, demonstrating that CELM generates reports that are more clinically coherent, diagnostically reliable, and better aligned with expert interpretation. We release our model code and benchmark construction pipeline at https://github.com/Jathurshan0330/CELM.
